title: Hou Yi, Chang'e and the Moon
objective: After this level you can retell the Chinese myth of the archer who shot down nine suns and the woman who flew to the Moon.
summary: In Chinese myth the archer Hou Yi shot down nine of ten burning suns. His wife Chang'e swallowed his elixir of immortality and fled to the Moon, honored at the Mid-Autumn Festival.

cards.headline: Ten suns in the sky at once, and the earth began to burn.
cards.body: In Chinese myth, ten suns were burning up the earth. The job of saving it fell to one man with a bow.

cards.headline: Nine arrows
cards.body: He was Hou Yi, the Lord Archer, whose skill with a bow earned him undying fame. He shot down 9 of the 10 suns, leaving the one we still have. Even here, tellings differ: one account says he shot 8 of 9. Myths don't come with one official edition.

cards.headline: The stolen elixir
cards.body: Hou Yi received an elixir of immortality from a great goddess, the Queen Mother of the West. Before he could take it, his wife Chang'e swallowed it herself and became immortal. Fearing his anger, she fled to the Moon, where she lives in the Palace of Boundless Cold. In paintings, a white rabbit beside her pounds the elixir with a mortar and pestle.

cards.fact: Look for Chang'e at the Mid-Autumn Festival.
cards.context: On the 15th day of the eighth lunar month, people celebrate Chang'e with the Mid-Autumn Festival and eat mooncakes, rich pastries with sweet or savory fillings. Some look for the outline of a toad on the Moon, because in one legend Chang'e became a toad. Her story isn't only in old books. It comes around every autumn.

cards.headline: Hou Yi and Chang'e: told
learned: Hou Yi shot down nine of ten suns
Myths come in more than one version
Chang'e swallowed the elixir and fled to the Moon

questions.prompt: In the best-known telling, Hou Yi shot down _____ suns.

options.label: all ten
options.rationale: He left one in the sky.

questions.explanation: Hou Yi shot down 9 of the 10 suns burning up the earth, leaving one (one account says 8 of 9).

questions.prompt: Match each figure from the myth with what goes with them.
questions.explanation: Hou Yi is the Lord Archer, Chang'e lives in the Palace of Boundless Cold on the Moon, and the white rabbit pounds the elixir with a mortar and pestle.

questions.prompt: In Level 3, a serpent took Gilgamesh's plant of youth. How does Chang'e's story turn that around?

options.label: A snake steals her elixir too
She gains immortality by swallowing the elixir
Hou Yi drinks it first and becomes a god

questions.explanation: Gilgamesh loses his chance and stays mortal; Chang'e swallows the elixir and becomes immortal.
